title: Protocol to photoactivate adipose-derived stem cell differentiation using a tightly-focused femtosecond laser
protocol: Sterilize the surgery tools and operation area.
Prepare the culture medium for ADSCs: BASIC MEM alpha culture medium (MEM-α) with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) and 1% Penicillin-Streptomycin (10,000 U/mL).
Euthanize 7-day postnatal male SD rats using methods approved by the animal welfare committee.
Spray the surface of the rats with 75% ethanol and place them in the operation area.
Dissect the adipose tissue of the groin and epididymal/parametrial fat pads.
Wash the adipose tissue in PBS buffer and mince them with a sterilized scissor.
Transfer the tissue to a 15 mL tube.
Mix it in the ratio of 1:1 (vol/vol) with 2% collagenase type I solution for digestion.
Incubate for 30–60 min at 37°C until few tissue clumps are visible.
Gently agitate the tube every 8-10 minutes for better mixing during digestion.
Add 2 mL of digestive termination buffer to the tube.
Dissociate cells by gently pipetting up and down.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 minutes at room temperature (25°C).
Discard the supernatant containing adipocytes and debris.
Resuspend cell pellets in 7 mL culture medium.
Filter the cell resuspension through a 70-μm cell strainer to obtain single-cell suspension of ADSCs.
Seed single cells at 1 × 10^6/mL into 100-mm culture dishes.
Incubate for 72 hours at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Passage the cells or refresh the medium every 2 days during normal culture and expansion.
Refresh the medium every 2 days after photoactivation for up to 21 days.
At cell confluency of 80%, take out the dishes for passaging and plating.
Wash cells with pre-warmed PBS buffer 3 times.
Add 1 mL of 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA for 30 seconds to digest ADSCs.
Add 2 mL of culture medium to terminate trypsinization.
Transfer the cell resuspension to a new 15-mL tube.
Centrifuge the tube at 300 × g for 5 minutes at room temperature (25°C).
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellets in culture medium to obtain a 3 × 10^5/mL cell suspension.
Carefully drop 5 μl of cell suspension at the center of a petri dish with a 15-mm glass bottom.
Place the dish in the incubator for 2 h at 37°C and 5% CO2 and wait for cells to adhere to the bottom.
Add another 2 mL culture medium gently and incubate it for 24 h before photoactivation.
Turn on the femtosecond laser source.
Ensure the shutter is closed.
Set the power of the femtosecond laser at 10–15 mW at the specimen.
Set the excitation laser at 543 nm at 0.5 mW for transmission bright-field microscopy.
Set imaging parameter at 800 × 800 pixels, 2.0 μs/pixel.
Set the correction collar of the objective at 0.17 mm.
Check the thickness of the glass bottom of the dishes.
Change the correction collar of the objective if the thickness is not 0.17 mm.
Put the dish with ADSCs on the microscope stage.
Tune the objective (60 ×, N.A. = 1.2) vertically for clear bright-field confocal images.
Switch to point-scanning mode and position the laser focus in the region of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) near the nucleus in the target cell.
Keep the imaging focal plane at the clearest topography in the brightfield image.
Ensure the femtosecond laser is focused inside the cell vertically if strictly collimated.
Calibrate the focus of the femtosecond laser with the imaging plane of the transmission bright-field microscopy.
Image a 3D standard sample using both the femtosecond laser and confocal fluorescent microscopy.
Adjust the objective to achieve identical images from both imaging methods.
Record the distance adjustment needed for image alignment.
Pre-set the mechanical shutter opening gate to 200 ms for each photoactivation cycle.
Start point-scanning with simultaneous single-time 200 ms photoactivation using a power of 10–15 mW at the specimen.
Move the scan point to the next cell and localize the laser focus on the ER region.
Repeat steps until all cells in the field of view are activated.
Shift the microscope stage to image the adjacent neighboring field of view.
Repeat steps from 28 to 30 for photoactivation of all cells across the entire dish.
Change the medium half an hour after the photoactivation experiment.
Culture the cells and change the cell medium every 2 days up to the 21st day after photoactivation.
Perform immunofluorescence microscopy to assess differentiated osteoblasts.
Conduct Alizarin Red S staining to evaluate differentiated osteoblasts.
Take out the dishes plated with photoactivated ADSCs from the incubator.
Wash each dish with 1 mL pre-warmed PBS three times.
Fix the cells with 2 mL pre-warmed 4% paraformaldehyde for 15 min.
Wash cells in PBST (PBS with 0.1% Tween 20) three times, five minutes each.
Treat the cells with 2 mL PBST containing 0.1% Triton X-100 for 15 min.
Wash cells in PBST three times, five minutes each.
Block non-specific adsorption of proteins with 2 mL 5% skim milk in PBST at room temperature for one hour.
Wash cells in PBST for three minutes.
Incubate the cells with 2 mL solution of Runx2 primary antibody (1:500 in PBST, rabbit) at 4°C overnight.
Wash each dish in PBST three times, five minutes each.
Capture images by confocal microscopy (excited by 473 or 488 nm laser).
Prepare Alizarin Red S solution by adding 1 g of alizarin red S powder to 50 mL of ddH2O.
Tune the pH value of the Alizarin Red S mixture to 4.2 with 10% NH4OH.
Filter the Alizarin Red S solution through a 0.22 μm strainer.
Store the prepared Alizarin Red S solution at 4°C in the dark for up to one month.
Take out dishes plated with photoactivated ADSCs from the incubator.
Wash cells three times with 1 mL pre-warmed PBS.
Fix cells with 2 mL pre-warmed 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) for 30 minutes.
Wash each dish three times, five minutes each in 1 mL ddH2O.
Treat cells with 2 mL Alizarin Red S solution for three minutes.
Wash each dish three times, five minutes each in 1 mL ddH2O.
Capture images of the treated dishes using a bright-field microscope.
Anesthetize the Math1-GFP; Dcx-DsRed double reporter mouse (20–25 days old, male) with isoflurane (1–2%) in 0.5–1.0 L/min of O2 during surgery.
Hold the mouse on a custom stainless steel mouse adapter.
Apply eye ointment to prevent mouse eyes from drying out.
Wipe the skin above the cerebellum with iodophor.
Remove the hair and skin above the cerebellum with sterilized ophthalmic scissors.
Use a scalpel to scrape the periosteum from the skull.
Carefully remove the muscles overlying the cerebellum.
Wipe the surface of the skull with saline mixed with penicillin.
Thin the localized skull about 2.0 mm caudal to lambda.
Grind the skull gently with a 0.5mm cranial drill until blood vessels are visible.
Remove the topmost bone layer with the cranial drill.
Drill through the middle layer of the skull to remove bone trabecula.
Grind the lowest layer of bone until the skull deforms with light touch.
Ensure the integrity of the skull is maintained without perforation or cracking.
Glue a custom stainless-steel head fixation plate anterior from lambda using dental cement.
Fix the stainless-steel plate to one end of the mouse adapter with medical tape.
Keep the mouse anesthetized during microscopy and photoactivation experiments.
Turn on the femtosecond laser source.
Turn on the confocal microscope.
Open the mechanical shutter.
Set the excitation lasers at 473 nm to 0.5 mW.
Set the excitation lasers at 543 nm to 0.8 mW.
Set the power of the femtosecond laser (1030 nm, ∼220 fs, 1 MHz) to 5 mW.
Place the pre-treated mouse on the microscope stage.
Move the stage to position the cerebellum under the objective.
Tune the water-immersed objective (60 ×, N.A. = 1.0) closely to the skull.
Ensure water on the objective contacts with the skull.
Run the fast-scanning mode of the confocal microscope.
Tune the objective vertically for a clear fluorescent image of neurons in the cerebellum.
Activate the GNPs in FOV one by one using a femtosecond laser at 5–10 mW for 200 ms.
Adjust the laser power based on the depth of GNPs, considering tissue scattering and absorption effects.
Re-localize the photoactivation region in steps 44–47.
Re-observe the photoactivated region in the cerebellum after 24 h.
Count GNs (red) and GNPs (green) in the re-observed region.
